nodes.title: PuLID Instructions
widgets_values: There are four images here for easy of use. Load your potential best images for the subject's face. When the workflow runs, it will show a score in the PuLID Analysis Preview.  You want a score of 0.90 or greater.  If you don't get a score of 0.90 or higher, change the input to the next image and try again. If none of your images score high enough, load 4 different images and try again.

nodes.title: Main workflow instructions
widgets_values:
From the Left of the workflow to right:

First:
Load four of your best face images in the PuLID Reference Images
Choose images with shots of chest to head or waist to head.  If they if the shot is too close, PuLID will not detect it. If it is too far, it will not score well for the analysis and will be a bad reference. You want a score of 0.90 or higher.

Second:
Choose how many reference images you wish to use and toggle off the Image Reference group you wish not to use. The labels on the image loaders are the recommended image shots to of your subject to use.  You do not have to follow this to the letter, and sometimes switching them up works better.  It's something you have to experiment with for best results. Keep in mind, the FIRST reference images have more weight than the last.

Third:
Fill out your Subdirectory and set your desired resolution.  The Image Resolution Resize is set so that the resolution will alwasy be a multiple of 16 (Flux2 Klein requirement). To raise or lower the image resolution, change the Megapixel value.

Fourth:
Set the MultiGPU settings to fit your computer system in the model loaders.  make sure the correct models are loaded in the model loaders.

Fifth:
Choose LoRAs in the LoraManager Loader and pick the trigger words in the TriggerWord Toggle Node. I have found, that PuLID+Reference Images+Character LoRA all working together, gives incredible consistency. 

Sixth:
Decide whether or not you want to run Phase 2 as a refiner and togle it off or on depending on what you decide.  The refinement is 100% LoRa and prompt based using Flux2 Klein KV as a photo editor to add detail or lighting, or whatever you want to do.  If you have a Character LoRA, this is a makes a great refining pass for your character. Also, you can choose to run the RAM and VRAM cleaners.  It will add time to the generation, but may save you from OOM errors.  

Seventh:
Put in your prompt.  The prompt node handles randomized promts in {option1|option2|option3} format and shows the prompt resolution in the second window of the node. If you are Using the same base model in both phases, it will only load the model once and you shouldn't have to use the cleaners group. 

Eighth:
Chose your uscale meathod or toggle off the upscale altogether.  If you have an NVidia RTX 2 or higher GPU, you can use the NVidia node.  If not, or if you prefer, you can use the Upscale By Model nodes.
